policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'where hast thou not been lain with?' renders the qere שֻׁכַּבְתְּ (pual of שכב, to lie with); the ketiv שגלת (shagal, to ravish) would give the coarser 'been ravished'. The euphemistic English matches the qere lemma.

ASV 'Wilt thou not from this time cry unto me' makes the addressee the subject, matching the 2fs qere קָרָאת; the ketiv קראתי is 1cs 'I called', which the ASV does not render. The only note here is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, companion') and bears on the following clause, not on this reading.

ASV 'thou hast spoken and hast done evil things' is second feminine singular, matching the qere דִבַּרְתְּ; the ketiv דברתי would be 1cs 'I have spoken'. Both notes are alternative_rendering and hebrew_gloss and do not touch the person of the verb.

Qere וַתֵּרֶא and ketiv ותראה differ only in the final ה of the defective/plene spelling of the same wayyiqtol of ראה; both yield 'and she saw'. ASV 'and her treacherous sister Judah saw it' is compatible with either, and the two notes on this verse are alternative_rendering, bearing on the framing of 'And I said' and on 'She will return', not on this verb.

ASV text reads 'Ye shall call me My Father', a masculine plural subject matching the ketiv תקראו; the 2fs qere תִּקְרְאִי would give 'Thou shalt call'. The note classed textual_variant, 'Another reading is, Thou shalt . . . and shalt not etc.', explicitly relegates the qere to the margin, confirming that the ASV text renders the ketiv.

The same textual_variant note, 'Another reading is, Thou shalt . . . and shalt not etc.', covers this verb as well as the preceding one, placing the 2fs qere תָשׁוּבִי in the margin; the ASV text 'and shall not turn away from following me' continues the plural subject 'Ye' and so renders the ketiv תשובו.
